items.title: Full transcript of "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Nov. 15, 2026
items.desc: On this "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" broadcast, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Sen. Bill Cassidy join Margaret Brennan.

items.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status as cases surge nationwide
items.desc: The United States has lost its official measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years. Here's what to know.

items.title: Chris Van Hollen Says His Majority Leader Challenge to Chuck Schumer Is Gaining Support
items.desc: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said on Sunday that he has a “wide-open” path to unseat Chuck Schumer, the long-serving Senate Democratic leader.

items.title: 8 Takeaways From a Big Democratic Gathering in Denver: Democrats in Array
items.desc: More than a half-dozen potential Democratic presidential candidates made early pitches for themselves and their visions at what amounted to a party-wide post-election victory party.

items.title: 'We slept here': Flight delays linger but schedule is back on track for Monday
items.desc: Flight disruptions lingered two days after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded departures nationwide for more than four hours.

items.title: Flight Delays and Cancellations Persist as System Recovers From Ground Stop
items.desc: Operations are returning to normal after air traffic was shut down for more than 4 hours on Friday following a maintenance upgrade that crippled communications.

items.title: DOT Sec. Duffy ties router in southern Arkansas to issues that led to nationwide ground stop
items.desc: The FAA ground stop came after updates to an older communication system managed by L3Harris Technologies, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.

items.title: ‘I Love Being a Girl’: Inside the Life of a Sorority Influencer
items.desc: Many young adults want to be influencers. And why not? It’s fun. But it also means that the camera is always on.

items.title: Bessent calls for ‘dramatic shakeup’ at Nvidia, urges outside CEO
items.desc: Bessent has criticized Howard Lutnick’s department over suspected chip diversion to China while defending President Donald Trump’s handling of the matter.

items.title: Sean Duffy Offers New Details on How One Fix Spiraled Into Nationwide Ground Stop
items.desc: When asked, the transportation secretary could not guarantee on Sunday that a similar air traffic meltdown would not occur again.

items.title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
items.desc: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.

items.title: Embattled Federal Employees Look to a Democratic Congress for a Lifeline
items.desc: Former and current workers have found a sympathetic ear among Democrats set to take over the House and Senate. But any reversal of President Trump’s cuts is unlikely to happen immediately.

items.title: Judge temporarily blocks closing of historic D.C. golf course
items.desc: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes ruled that the Trump administration cannot close East Potomac Park in Washington, D.C., for now.

items.title: Trump breaks silence about FAA nationwide ground stop, blames Biden administration
items.desc: Trump blamed the Biden administration for the FAA’s aging system after a nationwide ground stop disrupted air travel and urged Congress to approve more funding.

items.title: Ground stop shows "we have to get off old network," Duffy says
items.desc: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that "we have to get off old network, old telecom" after a telecommunication outage led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.

items.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Nov. 15)
items.desc: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

items.title: Two Planes Collide on a Taxiway at Miami International Airport
items.desc: The wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767, a day after a nationwide ground stop disrupted air travel.

items.title: What to Know About Continued Flight Disruptions
items.desc: After a nationwide ground stop Friday, travelers are still encountering snags, and it could take several days for flight schedules to return to normal.

items.title: Nature: Sea lions in La Jolla, Calif.
items.desc: We leave you this Sunday morning in the company of sea lions who call the waters off La Jolla, Calif., their home. Videographer: Carl Mrozek.

items.title: 11/15: Face The Nation
items.desc: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," as the effects of Friday's nationwide ground stop are still being felt, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy joins. Plus, as the U.S. loses its measles elimination status, Sen. Bill Cassidy, the chairman of the Senate Health Committee, joins.

items.title: 3 big things we're watching in the stock market in the week ahead
items.desc: Nvidia and Anthropic will share the spotlight in a pivotal week for the AI trade.

items.title: Judge Blocks Immediate Closure of East Potomac Park for Trump Golf Project
items.desc: Judge Ana C. Reyes, who has been overseeing combative litigation, said the Trump administration would not be responsible for operating the course while the case proceeded.

items.title: Flights expected to normalize by tonight after ground stop. Here's what to know
items.desc: Officials attributed the ground stop to aging system infrastructure and legacy technology.

items.title: Billy Evans calls his portrayal in Elizabeth Holmes documentary "crazy"
items.desc: Billy Evans, the partner of Elizabeth Holmes, opened up about his portrayal in a hit documentary on "CBS Sunday Morning."

items.title: Here's how Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation unfolded at Nvidia
items.desc: Jensen Huang's shocking exit as CEO of Nvidia unspooled suddenly, yet signs of trouble had emerged much earlier.

items.title: Outcome of Alaska Senate race could take weeks to determine
items.desc: The Senate race in Alaska, which has garnered widespread attention with two candidates named Dan Sullivan, remains in limbo.

items.title: Social Security and the blue wave: What could happen to payroll taxes and senior tax breaks
items.desc: Democrats advocated taxing high earners to shore up Social Security in the runup to the midterms. Plus, a senior deduction is slated to expire in two years.

items.title: The sinking of the SS United States
items.desc: Last Wednesday, the SS United States was sent to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico, to become the largest artificial reef in the world.

items.title: Aiding veterans with the healing arts
items.desc: With her in-person and virtual painting workshops and online tutorials, artist Mary Whyte teaches veterans to use art to deal with isolation and trauma through her "watercolor boot camps."

items.title: Aiding veterans with the healing arts
items.desc: With her in-person and virtual painting workshops and online tutorials, artist Mary Whyte teaches veterans to use art to deal with isolation and trauma through her "watercolor boot camps." Correspondent Martha Teichner reports on an arts program, now in 48 states, that helps veterans' self-expression, and allows them to reconnect with fellow vets, their communities – and themselves.

items.title: "November 1963": Did the mob kill JFK?
items.desc: A new film posits that the Kennedy assassination was tied to a Chicago crime boss, Sam Giancana. Screenwriter Nicki Celozzi, actor John Travolta, and Giancana's daughter, Bonnie, discuss the mob's alleged connection to a murder that changed the world.

items.title: "November 1963": Did the mob kill JFK?
items.desc: A new film, "November 1963," posits that the assassination of President John F. Kennedy was tied to a Chicago crime syndicate and its boss, Sam Giancana. Correspondent Lee Cowan talks with screenwriter Nicki Celozzi – Giancana's great-nephew – along with star John Travolta and Giancana's daughter, Bonnie, about the mob's alleged connection to a murder that changed the world.

items.title: 11/15: Sunday Morning
items.desc: Hosted by Jane Pauley. Featured: Did the mob kill JFK?; U2 at 50; Billy Evans on "You Can See Everything"; author Min Jin Lee; artist Mary Whyte; and the history of the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

items.title: I'm a psychologist who studies couples—5 signs you've fallen into a common rut: 'It builds through small habits that each look harmless'
items.desc: Couples today are vulnerable to "coexistence without contact," says psychologist Mark Travers. Here are the symptoms — and what you can do to counteract them.

items.title: Laws limiting coal miners' exposure to toxic dust are in danger of being rolled back
items.desc: Coal miners who are exposed to silica dust are at a higher risk of black lung disease. Despite decades of advocacy, new efforts to regulate the toxic dust are under threat.

items.title: Rivian, Lucid, Scout CEOs aren’t counting on Democrats to restore EV federal support after midterm wins
items.desc: EV makers have had to contend with flip-flopping regulatory support from Washington over the years.

items.title: Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on these 3 stocks for the long term
items.desc: Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks.

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO lands as the embattled AI trade looks for a much-needed bright spot
items.desc: Anthropic's IPO has outsized importance in the tech industry, which is heavily invested in the AI lab and is desperate for some positive momentum.

items.title: Lutnick Pushed to Weaken Chip Rules That Overlap With His Family Business
items.desc: The commerce secretary has been writing new rules that would affect Southeast Asian data centers, some of which are clients of his former firm.

items.title: After Midterms Triumph, Democrats Look Quickly and Eagerly Ahead to 2028
items.desc: Politicians, donors and campaign strategists are already imagining a large and contentious field of presidential contenders.

items.title: The Reward for Black Women’s Work in Georgia: Leaders Who Look Like Them
items.desc: Diligent ground-level efforts by Black women helped make Democrats competitive again in Georgia. Now they’ll hold seven of the top eight elected leadership roles in the state.

items.title: A Campus Sexual Assault Lawsuit Tests an Unusual Legal Strategy
items.desc: Frustrated by Texas Christian University’s handling of her sexual assault case, a former student from Virginia is suing under her home state’s consumer protection laws.

items.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
items.desc: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.

items.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
items.desc: The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today.

items.title: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
items.desc: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.

items.title: Oregon community suspects foul play when beloved shopkeeper disappears
items.desc: When Susan "Phoenix" Lane and her two dogs went missing from Welches, Oregon, in the foothills of Mount Hood, her friends and family suspected foul play almost immediately.

items.title: Could Budapest be the next digital nomad hotspot?
items.desc: With its mix of sights, cafés and culture, Hungary's capital Budapest has become popular with those embracing the "work from anywhere" trend.

items.title: Trump blasts judge for halting his Washington golf project and says he will appeal
items.desc: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.

items.title: How Trump administration responded to FAA ground stop
items.desc: President Trump was informed within 30 minutes after the Federal Aviation Administration imposed a nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon, according to U.S. officials.

items.title: After Her Baby Was Buried Alive, a South Carolina Mother Wonders Why
items.desc: Koah Sharp, nearly 1, was rescued alive this week in a rural patch of central South Carolina. In her first interview, Koah’s mother explains what happened.

items.title: Evacuation lifted after bomb threat near industrial plant in Illinois
items.desc: Police said the device had been rendered safe and residents were allowed to return to their homes.

items.title: FAA ground stop disrupts college football
items.desc: Some college football games were delayed a few hours on Saturday or postponed to Sunday. And in Oklahoma at least, there will be perks for fans to make up for the inconvenience, including cheap beers.

items.title: Unlike Other Countries, America’s Government Funds Its Air Infrastructure
items.desc: Despite handling the most flights in the world, the United States’ air traffic systems rely on 1980s-era computer equipment.

items.title: Stranded by planes, travelers turned to trains and automobiles.
items.desc: People trying to find new ways to get to their destinations still encountered obstacles at the rental car counter and on Amtrak’s booking system.

items.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law
items.desc: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run.

items.title: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
items.desc: Starship Test Flight 15 marked the first time Elon Musk's company tried to catch both the booster and upper stage of the rocket.

items.title: Passengers rescued after tanker hit river cruise in New Orleans
items.desc: A tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans Friday, partially submerging the passenger boat.

items.title: 'Root cause’ of nationwide ground stop is unknown, FAA says
items.desc: Routers and networking equipment may be involved in the problems that led to the ground stop, but a definitive cause has not been established, officials said.

items.title: Maintenance gone awry caused nation-wide ground stop, says Transportation Secretary
items.desc: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy points blame toward contractor in explaining Friday's nation-wide aviation ground stop.

items.title: $180 million Van Gogh tests the art market and collector confidence
items.desc: The art auctions in New York next week could top $2 billion, as a treasure trove of masterpieces comes to the market for the first time in decades.

items.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
items.desc: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.

items.title: Trump Kept Out of Sight as F.A.A. Issued Flight Ground Stop
items.desc: The F.A.A. called a rare halt on flights nationwide, but the president stayed away from cameras and issued social media posts on the entertainment industry and California’s Democratic governor.

items.title: Defense Contractor L3Harris Was Behind Upgrade That Led to Ground Stop
items.desc: The little-known defense giant does a lot of work for the Federal Aviation Administration and owns the equipment for the agency’s telecommunications network.

items.title: Democrats push back on Duffy’s demand for $50 billion to upgrade air traffic systems.
items.desc: Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, requested $50 billion from Congress to overhaul the American air traffic system.

items.title: Travel Nightmare Continues for Stranded Passengers Awaiting Flights
items.desc: After a night of fitful sleep on airport floors, some travelers are still stuck amid thousands of flight cancellations following Friday’s ground stop.

items.title: Dramatic video shows river boats colliding
items.desc: All aboard were accounted for after a cargo tanker crashed into a river cruise in New Orleans. CBS News' Skyler Henry reports.
